result.killer: No single killer was found. The weakness is market size: quotas of roughly 2-15% of Gabonese headcount, a paper-based ministry process run through fixers and law firms, and weak enforcement (the minister admitted a shortage of inspectors). The volume of small-employer applications is still unverified.
result.reason: I found no killer: no Gabonese software and no online Ministry of Labour, ONE or DGDI portal for work authorisations. The duty is real and has tightened. Décret 0150/PR/MTLCC of 21 March 2025 sets foreign-worker quotas by staff category (sources give 2-15%). It also charges 500,000 FCFA per application and ties renewal to delivering 80% of a training plan for a Gabonese counterpart. But the flow is paper-based and depends on contacts at the ministry: an ONE "attestation de carence", contracts signed by the labour inspector, and files lodged at the Minister's cabinet. Law firms and local fixers already handle it. Quotas are counted against Gabonese headcount, so a small firm can hire very few foreigners. That likely means low volume per buyer, and the ministry admits it lacks inspectors. The claim also cites Code 3/94, which the 2021 Code repealed.

candidates.trigger: LF2026 art. P-832 ter CGI. Sources differ on dates: mandatory from 1 Jan 2026, or accepted for VAT recovery and deductions only from 1 Jul 2026. Penalties: 100% of the transaction value (minimum 200,000 FCFA) for a missing invoice, 50,000 FCFA for an incomplete one, up to 10M FCFA per invoice for repeat offences, plus possible closure. Platform: DIGITAX.
candidates.unchecked: Not rechecked. Supporting evidence for K01 only; the deadline and penalties are now confirmed from Deloitte and press.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: A 2025 arrete (number/date unverified; Miranda legal news Mar-Apr 2025) covers all LPG distributors and filling centres: international manufacturing standards, traceability marking, regular safety inspections, requalification of cylinders every 5 years, max life 25 years, strict filling conditions, 12 months for existing operators to comply. New filling centres (SGEPP Port-Gentil Apr 2026, Moanda project) signal growth. Fuel-station-specific duties not found. Candidate C4.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Gabon cocoa output is only ~100-200 t/year; no Gabon exporter-licensing decree found (CASTAIB mentioned as the stabilisation fund, unverified). Nothing buildable. Candidate C13 (weak).

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Microfinance (EMF) falls under CEMAC/COBAC regulation 01/17/CEMAC/UMAC/COBAC (regional). Only about 18 EMFs are based in Gabon out of 521 in CEMAC, so the buyer pool is too small. No Gabon COOPEC reporting rule found. Fishing cooperatives (Gab Peche) noted under 35.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K04 for CNAMGS claims. Pharmacies (Sypharga) suspended CNAMGS service in Jan 2025 and issued a new ultimatum in Oct-Nov 2025 over multi-billion FCFA arrears, which is evidence of pain for K04. Nothing found on private clinics specifically.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: Regulator is ANMAPS, which trained inspectors in Feb 2026 across import, wholesale and retail. A 30% import-reduction policy favours local maker LSP, and wholesalers sit on the generics commission. LF2026 removes the VAT exemption on pharmaceutical products (new filing and invoicing duty). Candidate C7. Controlled chemicals/precursors: nothing found.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Labour provision (mise a disposition) firms: 125 registered, 94 in breach, one month to regularise from 29 March 2024, inspectors sent. Interim agencies need Ministry of Labour approval and a financial guarantee (guide source, flagged 'to verify'). 93 private security firms under authorisation review by the Interior Ministry commission on 23 June 2026 (known K06). Nothing specific found on cleaning firms. Candidate C2.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: Subcontracting ordinance 003/2021 (ratified by law 024/2021), mining local-development decree 0023/PR/MPGM of 22 Jan 2021, and Eramet Comilog reporting 75% of purchases in Gabon. No SME-level register, accreditation or reporting duty found. Candidate C9 (weak, unverified).

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: Law 006/2017 of 9 Aug 2017 regulates estate agents (professional card, campaign closed 31 Dec 2019). It is poorly enforced, and press calls for a public national register and for rules on 'demarcheurs'. CEMAC AML rules require suspicious-transaction reports to ANIF (secondary source). Nothing found on notaries. Candidates C5 and C6.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Tourism law 034/2020 (22 Mar 2021) covers lodging, travel agencies, tour operators and guides under CITAT and defines the agrement. No taxe de sejour or fiche de police rule found. AGATOUR is setting up local tourist offices (Feb 2025 workshop). LF2026: VAT exemption on tourism equipment investments of 300M FCFA or more drops to 5%. Candidate C10 (unverified).

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K03 for timber and EUDR. The Nkok SEZ has 217 processing plants (2023). A BEAC forecast shows timber output falling in 2026. No fish-export or cocoa registration rule found.

coverage.category: 31. Foreign-worker quotas and work authorisations (decree 0150/PR/MTLCC, 21 Mar 2025)
coverage.found: Quotas for foreign staff in private firms, with exemption terms, a 500,000 XAF fee on each initial and renewal application, and renewal conditional on 80% delivery of the Gabonese counterpart's training plan. Rates differ by source (10/15/2% per Miranda; 15/10/5% per Paul Hastings). Enforcement expected to tighten in 2026. Candidate C1.

coverage.category: 32. Subcontracting regime (ordinance 003/2021)
coverage.found: Defines capacity and specialty subcontracting. Registration or approval mechanics unverified; full text paywalled (LEDAF 2021 n 8). Candidate C9.

coverage.category: 33. General commerce law 005/2025 (26 Mar 2025) and regulated trade
coverage.found: Applies to anyone trading, producing, distributing or providing services. Requires commercial registration, technical approval from the sector ministry for regulated activities (art. 7), and a 90% Gabonese-employee quota for foreign-run firms. Existing operators have 12 months to comply (about March 2026, from publication on 28 Mar 2025). Press says implementing decrees are missing. Candidate C8.

coverage.category: 34. Finance Law 2026 (law 041/2025): rent withholding, TFH, CFU, patente, excise
coverage.found: Rent withholding rises from 5% to 10%, paid quarterly within 15 days of quarter-end. Taxe forfaitaire d'habitation (500-30,000 FCFA a month for individuals, 1,000-50,000 for businesses) is collected by SEEG on the power bill, so there is no filing. CFU extended nationwide (3% for individuals, 15% flat for legal entities). Patente is 0.1% of turnover with a 150k-10M FCFA range, paid by 1 March. New excise on beer, soft drinks, packaging, motorcycles, arms. Candidates C3, C11, C12.

coverage.category: 35. Artisanal fishing and fish value chain
coverage.found: Arrete 00009/MAEPSA/SG/DCAJ sets up a commission to grant artisanal fishing authorisations and industrial licences. Gab Peche pilot (Aug 2025) gave pirogues to fishing cooperatives. ANPN seizes engines for fishing in protected zones. LF2026 puts 5% VAT on fuel for artisanal fishing. Candidate C14 (weak).

coverage.category: 36. Microfinance, hospitality-tax and excise-liable small producers (LF2026 excise)
coverage.found: The only new item is the LF2026 excise on local beer, soft drinks and packaging, which hits a small number of producers and importers. Thin evidence. Folded into C12.

result.competitor: No Gabonese software and no online state portal for work authorisations were found. The only state platform found is the entry e-visa (since 2015). Today this work is done by law firms and HR/EOR vendors (Miranda, Playroll, Velocity Global, Globalization Partners) and by local fixers, all aimed at larger or international employers.
result.duty: Yes, the duty is real and in force. Under Décret n° 0162/PR/MTE of 7 March 2016, every employer of a foreign worker, whatever its legal form, needs an individual work authorisation (autorisation individuelle d'emploi) for a named post and company. Renewal must be started before the authorisation expires, and the employer must first show that no suitable Gabonese worker is available. Labour Code article 137 (loi 022/21 of 19 Nov 2021) led to Décret n° 0150/PR/MTLCC of 21 March 2025, published in JO n° 61 bis on 2 April 2025. It adds quotas by staff category, exemptions of 2 years renewable once that require training a Gabonese counterpart, renewal only once at least 80% of that training plan is delivered, and a non-refundable fee of XAF 500,000 for each first application or renewal. Frequency: once per hire, then renewal every 1-2 years (sources disagree: 6 months, 12 months, 2 years, 2-5 years). Penalties: not found. The ministry has said it lacks inspectors, so enforcement is weak. The claim's main source, Africarrieres, cites the old 1994 code and a decree '1116/PR/MTEPS' that could not be confirmed.
result.market: Unverifiable. No figures were found on authorisations issued or on how many employers hold foreign staff. There are probably a few thousand employers, including West African and Lebanese-owned SMEs, oil and mining subcontractors and staffing firms. As one example of the staffing segment, the ministry flagged 94 staffing firms (entreprises de mise à disposition) for not following the rules.
result.reason: The duty is real and was tightened in 2025: quotas, counterpart-training plans, an 80% training threshold before renewal and a XAF 500k fee per file. That supports a tracker covering expiry dates, quotas and training plans. However, filing is on paper, so software cannot submit anything. Renewals come only every 1-2 years. Enforcement is weak. Firms with real exposure usually pay lawyers or fixers, and the market is small and not measured. A done-for-you filing service with a simple expiry and quota tracker is the most realistic angle, but it is a niche business that depends on relationships. No competitor software was found.

Duty is real but municipal, not national. Owendo's 2026 campaign requires taxis, TM and clandos to complete the vehicle inspection and pay municipal tax, property tax and patente, then affix the vignette. The window is 1 Jan to 31 Mar per the Syltteg president, and the mayor had not set an official cutoff. Penalties are unspecified fines and a possible circulation ban. Libreville separately runs an annual QR vignette campaign with Moov Africa (2026 ceremony 28 May); that app only verifies vehicles. I found no owner-side deadline tracker, though my search was narrow. Market size was not checked. Weak points: small fleets, thin margins, a once-a-year event per commune, informal operators, and differing rules per commune. The DGTT agrément applicability is unchecked. Low score.

The announcements are real (7 Sept 2026: all gold via the Nkok refinery, QR-coded ingots, no buying from individuals, only via official comptoirs). Gabonreview cites no decree and no deadline. The only text found is decree 276/PR/MM of 2 June 2024, which routes artisanal gold through official circuits, notably SEM comptoirs. SEM is the sole operator and the QR system is state-run, so private comptoirs are probably not licensed. I found no private buyer base, no register and no competitor. Small-scale mining has been suspended since June 2026. The buyer group is tiny or absent and the tracking system is built by the state, so the commercial case is weak. Only 1 search ran. Competition and market size were not checked.

Duty is real: AGASA communiqués (Jan 2026) cite art. 7 of decree 0578/PR/MAEAMOPG (26 Nov 2015). Only food from establishments with a valid sanitary approval counts as compliant. Enforcement is by provisional closure and seizure. An AGASA desk at the ANPI-Gabon one-stop shop issues approvals in 2 to 7 days if the file is complete. No online portal and no competing software were found, but only one search was run. Not found: the renewal period, fees, full document list and exact scope (retail vs processors). Arrêté 008/MAEPA could not be opened (403). The approval looks like an infrequent, one-off file, not a recurring workflow. Buyers are informal and the willingness to pay is weak. The market size is not quantified.

Press confirms the 2024 Ministry of Labour audit: 125 registered firms, 94 non-compliant, one-month order from 29 Mar 2024, fines and prison cited. No law or decree is named, and the approval documents are only vaguely described (technical approval, "fiche circuit"). I found no lasting register or recurring filing cycle. This looks like a one-off enforcement push, not a recurring workflow. I found no competing software. The pool is about 125 firms, which is too small for a SaaS product. The CNSS/CNAMGS and 18-month claims are unverified. Not reached: Labour Code text, competitor search beyond one query.

Duty is real: law 041/2025 (29 Dec 2025) raises the rent withholding (art. 178 bis CGI) from 5% to 10%. Collection is quarterly, within 15 days of quarter-end, and applies to tenants that are companies, agencies or public bodies. The CFU is a separate annual owner tax, not withheld, so the "CFU remittance" part of the claim is partly mislabelled. A 2026 LFR (law 002/2026) exists, and I did not find whether it changed these rules. No competing software or DGI portal specific to this duty turned up, but I did not find the DGI e-filing details either. The market is small and fragmented, the payer is usually an accountant, there is one quarterly filing, and willingness to pay is low. The number of agencies is unquantified. Keep the score at 3.

The duty is attested only by a law-firm newsletter (Miranda Alliance, Mar-Apr 2025). It says an arrete covers all LPG distributors and filling centres, with 5-year requalification, a 25-year life, traceability marking and a 12-month transition. I found no official text, number or date, so I could not confirm it is in force. The buyer pool looks tiny. Press names only SGEPP (which took over Vivo), Petro Gabon and a few new filling centres (Port-Gentil opened 13 Apr 2026, Moanda and Owendo planned). These are large or state-linked firms, not small businesses. I found no official operator count. Requalification is a physical test, not software work. I did not search for competing software, so I can neither confirm nor rule it out. Score is low because of the thin buyer base and weak software fit.
